record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.original_question: Given a smooth twist diffeomorphism with a rotational invariant curve that is not smooth, can that invariant curve be destroyed by an arbitrarily small C^∞ perturbation?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1.2 (J. Mather) Given a Coo twist diffeomorphism and a ro­ tational invariant curve which is not Coo is it possible to destroy it by an arbitrarily small Coo perturbation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f\colon \mathbb{A} \to \mathbb{A}$ be a $C^\infty$ twist diffeomorphism of the annulus $\mathbb{A} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}$ (i.e., a diffeomorphism isotopic to the identity which, when lifted to $\mathbb{R}^2$, satisfies the monotone twist condition $\partial \tilde f_1/\partial y > 0$, where $\tilde f(x,y) = (\tilde f_1(x,y), \tilde f_2(x,y))$). A rotational invariant curve for $f$ is an $f$-invariant homotopically nontrivial simple closed curve in $\mathbb{A}$; by Birkhoff's theorem, any such curve is the graph of a Lipschitz function over the base circle.

Suppose that $f$ possesses a rotational invariant curve $\Gamma$ which is not of class $C^\infty$. Determine whether, for every neighborhood $\mathcal{U}$ of $f$ in the $C^\infty$ topology on the space of diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{A}$, there exists $g \in \mathcal{U}$ such that $g$ has no rotational invariant curve in a neighborhood of $\Gamma$ (equivalently, the invariant curve $\Gamma$ can be destroyed by an arbitrarily small $C^\infty$ perturbation).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a problem attributed to J. Mather concerning destruction of non-smooth invariant curves of smooth twist diffeomorphisms. Mather and others have established destruction results for invariant circles of given (Liouville or other) rotation numbers, and there is a substantial body of work on quantitative destruction. However, the precise statement—whether any rotational invariant curve that fails to be $C^\infty$ can be destroyed by an arbitrarily small $C^\infty$ perturbation—does not appear to have a clearly recorded full resolution in the sources found. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Destruction of invariant circles
status_evidence.snippet: For exact area-preserving monotone twist diffeomorphisms, if ω is Liouville, there exist arbitrarily close C∞ diffeomorphisms with no invariant circle of rotation number ω.
status_evidence.claim: Partial destruction results are known in the C∞ category for prescribed Liouville rotation numbers, but this does not directly address destruction of an arbitrary non-smooth invariant curve.

status_evidence.title: Quantitative destruction of invariant circles
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative relations among perturbation degree, regularity, perturbation size, and arithmetic properties of frequency for non-existence of invariant circles.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study destruction of invariant circles, indicating the area is active and the specific Mather problem is not declared resolved.
